questions.prompt: Why is epsilon-greedy poor at finding a sparse reward far away?
options: It has no memory of where it has been, so it acts like a random walk and revisits places
It always picks the greedy action, so it never takes any exploratory step at all
It needs a learned model of the environment, which a sparse reward does not provide
It uses too large a discount factor, so a far reward is always valued at zero
questions.explanation: Memoryless noise gives diffusive coverage, about distance squared steps.

questions.prompt: Count bonus beta/sqrt(n) with beta=0.5 and n=16. Value? (3 decimals)
UCB1 value Q + c sqrt(ln t / N) with Q=0.4, c=2, t=100, N=4. Value? (2 decimals)
In the noisy-TV problem a prediction-error bonus fails because:
options: The network is too small, so it can never reduce the error on any frame
Pure noise stays unpredictable, so the error and the bonus never decay
The bonus is always negative whenever the screen contains random noise
Noise lowers the discount factor, so the bonus is discounted away to nothing
questions.explanation: Aleatoric randomness cannot be learned away, so error stays high.

questions.prompt: Two coin hypotheses (heads probability 0.2 or 0.8), prior 0.5/0.5. Expected information gain of one flip in bits? (3 decimals)
Hypotheses (heads probability 0.5 or 0.5), prior 0.5/0.5. Information gain of a flip in bits?
questions.explanation: Both hypotheses predict the same data, so posterior = prior: 0 bits.

questions.prompt: Which quantity is best suited to ignore pure environment noise when rewarding exploration?
options: Expected information gain about the model parameters
The entropy of the policy's action distribution
Visit counts computed over the raw pixel observations
Raw next-frame prediction error on the observed pixels
questions.explanation: Information gain is zero when observations are independent of the unknown parameters.

questions.prompt: You add an RND-style novelty bonus to a mobile robot and its task return drops. Describe the evaluation you would run to find out why, including one noise-injection test and what you would report.
rubric: Report extrinsic return and an exploration statistic separately across seeds.
Noise-injection test: add an unpredictable source and check whether behaviour collapses to it.
Compare against epsilon-greedy and a decaying bonus; check that the bonus decays on repeated true states.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
